title: "Resources: Deviations and nonconformances"

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the SOP-requirement regulation, including paragraph (b)'s clause on written procedures for
  product-deviation investigations, quoted in this lesson. The local verbatim copy used here lives
  at `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the biological product deviation reporting rule this lesson applies to Owen Pruitt's donation.
  Already the full subject of the `risk-and-controls-vocabulary` foundation lesson; use this as a
  stable, citable mirror of the same text. Local copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[21 CFR 630.10 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/630.10)**
  — general donor eligibility requirements, including paragraph (h) (must not collect from a
  deferred donor) and the travel-history eligibility factor in paragraph (e)(2)(iii), both quoted
  or cited in this lesson. Local copy: `sources/cfr/630.10.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection, useful as a fallback primary
  source if a specific eCFR or Cornell page is ever unreachable, and for pulling an official PDF of
  a full CFR part when you need one for the record.
